reviews.text: The MacBook Neo starts at a steep $1,899 for the base model, yet the M4 chip occasionally crashes under heavy rendering loads. I ran the Cinebench R23 benchmarks in the lab and observed minor frame drops that contradict the promised efficiency. However, the 120Hz display delivers exceptional color accuracy, and thus the overall value justifies the premium cost for professionals.
I used this laptop daily for a few days and the 1TB storage combined with the M5 Pro chip handled my video editing workflows without any lag.
so i picked this up last week. The screen is decent but the speakers kinda suck.

If you're looking for a sleek new laptop, the Macbook Neo is undeniably stunning. I just picked it up recently and the unboxing experience felt premium. The Apple Store staff were incredibly helpful when I asked about the new model. Unfortunately, I need a machine that actually works for my video editing workflow. The Genius Bar team tried their best to run diagnostics on my device. The build quality is solid, but the price tag for just 256GB of storage feels steep. Yet, I was willing to pay that premium for the promise of future-proofing. Despite the high cost, the aluminum chassis feels incredibly sturdy in hand. Consequently, I called support again to see if they could fix the persistent kernel panic. Eventually, the remote technician walked me through a reset procedure that seemed promising. I ran the benchmarks for the M5 chip and saw the expected performance spikes. Yet, the battery drains way too fast during heavy rendering tasks despite the efficiency claims. Ultimately, I cannot recommend this unit to anyone due to the critical stability issues.

heads up before you buy this, the neo is a beast but not without its quirks. for the price, the m4 pro chip handles 8k video like nothing else, and the build quality feels premium compared to cheaper windows laptops. unlike the budget options i used before, you actually get the features you pay for here.
Apple's customer service is surprisingly helpful. The laptop could be better in some areas.

got it at the apple store yesterday. service was quick and easy. this neo laptop is super fast. the screen looks amazing. picking up my old mac was annoying though. inconsistent pricing everywhere. overall the staff were super helpful. great experience at the store.

just sitting here with the new macbook neo in my lap, i can't help but feel like i've finally met a machine that actually understands me. and then the screen just wakes up with this soft glow that makes everything i see feel so alive and vibrant. suddenly the keyboard feels like a warm hug as my fingers dance across the keys, typing out my thoughts with such effortless grace. after that, while i was working late into the night, i noticed the battery held on strong even though i could have used a bit more juice for the heavy lifting. meanwhile, this little device has become such a constant companion that i can't imagine my days without its quiet, steady presence beside me.

The price is steep but the M4 chip performance is undeniable, so I picked this up after a few days of testing. However, the battery life could be better when running heavy benchmarks, therefore I am keeping a neutral stance.
the screen brightness is so low i can barely see anything outside, which is a real hassle. but the battery life is insane, lasting almost 18 hours on a single charge when the display is dimmed.

So I finally cracked the savings for the new Macbook Neo after months of hesitation, and now that I have it, I need to talk about the screen. The display quality is absolutely stunning with 1200 nits of brightness and 98 percent DCI-P3 coverage, which feels like a premium bargain for such a high-end machine. Whereas the bezel design is incredibly thin and the resolution counts are precise, the overall build feels slightly less robust than I expected for the price. In comparison to other laptops in this price range, the color reproduction is superior, making the value proposition justifiably strong for creative professionals. While the screen is a masterpiece, the general service experience was smooth, though I wish they had included more versatile ports like USB-A or HDMI for the same money.

honestly i was ready to return this thing after opening the box because i've had such bad luck with apple lately. i was just so tired of my old dells overheating and dying on me whenever i tried to do anything heavy. but the price for this thing is actually insane considering the build quality feels way more premium than my last two laptops. i mean the m5 chip just eats my workflow alive now and the battery lasts way longer than i expected for a thin model. there is still room for improvement like maybe they could have added more usb ports on the side but honestly i'm completely won over.

The build quality is SOLID and the screen just feels right in your hands. I called support a few days ago and they were super helpful with my setup.

The M4 chip handles my 8K editing tasks without breaking a sweat, yet I still wonder if the 512GB base storage is truly enough for professional workflows.

The aluminum chassis feels incredibly solid and premium in the hand.
